paragraphs:
R' Shimon ben Menasya. In Mishnah Hagigah, first chapter, “70a”: he said, “‘What is crooked cannot be repaired …’; R' Shimon ben Yohai says ….” Thus he disputes R' Shimon ben Yohai and is placed before him. In Avot, chapter 6, he reports in R' Shimon ben Yohai's name. In Jerusalem Ma'aser Sheni, end of chapter 2: “The holy congregation: R' Yose ben Meshullam and R' Shimon ben Menasya.” Yuhasin writes under yod, at R' Yose ben Meshullam: R' Yose ben Meshullam is the holy congregation and preceded Rabbi's time; see his entry. But R' Shimon ben Menasya does not belong to the holy congregation, as appears in Ein Tzadin from Rashi's words, his questions, and the plain sense of the passage. At the end of Sefer Keritut, however, it appears that “they were much older than he” refers only to R' Meir: R' Shimon ben Menasya and his colleagues said that the halakhah follows R' Meir, and they were older—that is, than R' Meir. This suits the foregoing Jerusalem Talmud, which says that R' Shimon ben Menasya and R' Yose ben Meshullam are the holy congregation. But the evidence from Rashi is strong, for R' Shimon ben Menasya lived in Rabbi's time and disputed him over a firstborn animal. Likewise in Avot, chapter 6, he says that the seven qualities enumerated by the sages for the righteous were fulfilled in Rabbi and his sons. Likewise R' Yose ben Meshullam disputes R' Shimon ben Elazar, R' Meir's pupil. According to the Jerusalem Talmud, however, both are the holy congregation, and R' Meir would be older than they. End of quotation.

To make this clear to you, I shall copy the Gemara and Rashi at the beginning of Ein Tzadin, 26 end of side a. The rabbis taught: concerning an unblemished firstborn that fell into a pit, R' Yehudah the Nasi—Rashi: Rabbi—says that an expert should go down and inspect it; if it has a blemish, it may be brought up and slaughtered, and so forth. R' Shimon ben Menasya said to him, “They have already said that blemishes are not inspected on a festival.” Rashi explains: by “they have already said,” R' Shimon ben Menasya meant the preceding generations, for R' Shimon ben Yohai belonged to the generations before them, and Rabbi was his pupil. R' Shimon ben Menasya told Rabbi that earlier generations had disputed it and they should act strictly. For there in the Mishnah, R' Yehudah—that is, bar Illai—disputes: he says that an expert should go down and inspect a firstborn that fell into a pit; if it has a blemish, it may be brought up and slaughtered. R' Shimon says that anything whose blemish was not recognizable before the festival is not among what was prepared. End of the Mishnah.

There, 27a: R' Yehudah the Nasi had a firstborn animal and sent it before R' Ammi, who thought not to inspect it. R' Zerika said, “R' Yehudah versus R' Shimon—the halakhah follows R' Yehudah ….” He answered, “R' Shimon's view is more plausible ….” What was the conclusion? Rav Yosef said, “Come and hear, for it hangs on great ropes”—Rashi: great sages said it, and it is not easy to annul their words. For R' Shimon ben Pazi said in R' Yehoshua ben Levi's name, who said in R' Yose ben Shaul's name: Rabbi said in the name of the holy congregation in Jerusalem that R' Shimon and his colleagues—Rashi: R' Shimon ben Menasya and his colleagues, those who said, “They have already said that blemishes are not inspected on a festival”—said that the halakhah follows R' Meir, concerning firstborn animals. It now implies that the holy congregation testifies about R' Shimon ben Menasya, that he too said this. “Said? But they were much older than he!” Rashi explains that Rav Yosef expounds “said” as a question: is it possible that the holy congregation says that R' Shimon ben Menasya and his colleagues ruled according to R' Meir, so we act accordingly? They were much earlier and older than he! The holy congregation, in whose name Rabbi said this teaching, were much older than R' Shimon ben Menasya, who lived in the time of Rabbi and his sons, as we learn in Avot: R' Shimon ben Menasya said, “These seven qualities were fulfilled in Rabbi and his sons.” Above too he disputed him. How could the holy congregation state a law in R' Shimon ben Menasya's name, as it teaches, “R' Shimon and his colleagues said that the halakhah follows R' Meir”? Rather, they stated it in R' Meir's approach. That is, the holy congregation meant that R' Shimon ben Menasya and his colleagues who said not to inspect spoke in R' Meir's approach. It is possible for elders to consider young scholars' words and say that so-and-so's words incline toward an earlier R' so-and-so's words. This is what “it hangs on great ropes” means: the holy congregation said that R' Shimon's ruling accords with R' Meir's, so they stand in one approach. R' Yehudah is consequently alone, and one person's words have no standing against two. Rashi. Now you will understand Sefer Yuhasin's intention.

In Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Ha-Nehnakin, halakhah 4 [the checked edition has the passage at Sanhedrin 11:3:5]: R' Shimon ben Menasya says that beauty, strength, wealth, honor, wisdom, old age, and children are fitting for the righteous and fitting for the world, and so forth. It was taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says that all these seven qualities enumerated by the sages in the righteous were fulfilled in Rabbi and his sons. R' Yohanan said that all seven qualities the sages spoke of concerning the righteous were in Rabbi. Who is Rabbi? Rabbi is R' Yehudah the Nasi. R' Avahu said: Rabbi is R' Yudan the Nasi; he is our master. End of quotation. Thus according to this Jerusalem passage, R' Shimon ben Menasya did not say that the seven qualities were fulfilled in Rabbi. It follows its own view that R' Shimon ben Menasya and R' Yose ben Meshullam were the holy congregation, and Sefer Keritut's explanation that they were older than R' Meir. But in Pirkei Avot, as quoted by Rashi, R' Shimon ben Menasya said this. Perhaps there is an omission: R' Shimon ben Menasya said “beauty and strength …,” and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said about that that they were fulfilled in Rabbi, meaning his father Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh, who was called simply Rabbi; see R' Tarfon. R' Yohanan said that they were also fulfilled in Rabbi and his sons, meaning R' Yehudah the Nasi. This can be said with difficulty. But we find explicitly above that R' Shimon ben Menasya disputed Rabbi. This evidence brought by Rashi, that he lived in Rabbi's days, has no answer. It requires examination: Shimon ha-Temani was his disputant, see his entry, and R' Shimon ben Yehudah reports in his name; see whether these lived in Rabbi's days. He disputes R' Yose son of R' Yehudah and R' Yonatan ben Yosef; see his entry. Resh Lakish reports in his name: Niddah 45b; Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 20. R' Shimon ben Elazar said in R' Meir's name, and R' Shimon ben Menasya likewise said according to his words, “Why did they say that a dough is disqualified for the priesthood?”: Tosefta Kiddushin, chapter 5.
